title_en: Opinions of the Supreme People's Court on Providing Judicial Guarantees by the People's Courts for Building a Socialist New Countryside
full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Opinion on Providing Judicial Guarantees for the Building of a New Socialist Countryside by the People's Courts

Fa Fa [2006] No. 17

In order to implement the strategic deployment of the Fifth Plenary Session of the Sixteenth Central Committee of the Communist Party of China and to better give play to the adjudicative functions of the people's courts, the following opinion is hereby put forward regarding further improving the trial of agriculture-related cases and providing strong judicial guarantees for building a new socialist countryside.

I. Fully Understand the Great Significance of Further Improving the Trial of Agriculture-Related Cases

1. People's courts at all levels shall, by adopting various forms, organize adjudicators and other staff to conscientiously study the documents of the Sixteenth National Congress of the Party and the Third, Fourth, and Fifth Plenary Sessions of the Sixteenth Central Committee, as well as the "Several Opinions of the Central Committee of the Communist Party of China and the State Council on Promoting the Building of a New Socialist Countryside," deeply understand the rich connotation and spiritual essence of the relevant policies and measures of the Party and the State, and fully recognize the necessity and urgency of building a new socialist countryside and its major historical significance in China's modernization process. From the guiding principles of implementing the "Three Represents" important thought, establishing the Scientific Outlook on Development, adhering to the socialist rule of law concept, and upholding the work policy of "impartial justice and wholehearted service to the people," we shall further raise the awareness of the importance of strengthening the trial of agriculture-related cases. In light of local actual conditions, practical and feasible specific measures shall be formulated to establish institutional safeguard mechanisms for the full play of the various adjudicative functions of the people's courts in the process of building a new socialist countryside.

II. Strengthen Case Filing, Trial, and Enforcement Work for Agriculture-Related Cases

2. For all types of agriculture-related dispute cases that meet the conditions for case filing, they shall be promptly filed according to law, and efforts shall be made to file on the same day and transfer them in a timely manner. The provisions of the Supreme People's Court's "Decision on Comprehensively Strengthening the Work of People's Tribunals" regarding "direct acceptance of cases by people's tribunals" shall be earnestly implemented, truly providing guarantees from the system and mechanism to facilitate the filing of lawsuits by the vast number of farmers.

3. The work of litigation risk notification shall be implemented, judicial relief shall be increased, and for farmer parties who meet the conditions for deferral, reduction, or exemption of litigation costs and have submitted corresponding applications, they shall be allowed to defer, reduce, or exempt litigation costs.

4. The following crimes that endanger rural social stability, sabotage agricultural production, harm farmers' interests, or jeopardize rural democratic governance shall be resolutely punished according to law, and full efforts shall be made to safeguard agricultural production development and rural social stability:

(1) Crimes of producing and selling counterfeit and shoddy pesticides, veterinary drugs, fertilizers, seeds, and other agricultural means of production;

(2) Crimes of using official positions to intercept, misappropriate, or embezzle state agricultural fiscal subsidies, agricultural production inputs, rural social security funds, land expropriation compensation funds, and various agricultural relief funds and materials for disaster relief, emergency rescue, flood control, special care, and poverty alleviation, as well as crimes of embezzling rural collective and individual property;

(3) Crimes of organized crime of a mafia nature and crimes of vicious forces and gangs;

(4) Crimes of illegally transferring or reselling land use rights, illegally occupying cultivated land, or illegally approving expropriation or occupation of land;

(5) Crimes of gambling using "Mark Six" or other methods;

(6) Crimes of sabotage to elections;

(7) Crimes of damaging farmland irrigation, electricity, and other production and living facilities;

(8) Other crimes that seriously endanger agricultural production, rural social order, or infringe upon farmers' rights and interests.

5. In light of the actual circumstances of farmer parties, the work of litigation guidance shall be effectively strengthened to provide assistance for parties in agriculture-related cases in correctly exercising their litigation rights and reasonably taking litigation actions.

6. In the trial of various types of disputes over rural land contracting, the "Rural Land Contracting Law," the Supreme People's Court's "Interpretation on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Cases Involving Disputes over Rural Land Contracting," and other relevant laws and judicial interpretations shall be strictly applied to protect according to law the various land contracting and management rights and interests of farmers, including migrant workers.

7. Where the facts of a case are clear and the legal relationship is unambiguous, and a farmer party applies for property preservation but has genuine difficulty in providing a guarantee, and failure to take preservation measures may cause damage to the applicant's interests, the people's court may exempt the applicant from the guarantee obligation and rule to take property preservation measures.

8. In the trial of the following civil cases, where the statutory conditions for advance enforcement are met, the people's court shall promptly rule on advance enforcement:

(1) Disputes over damages where farmers request compensation for losses caused by counterfeit and shoddy agricultural materials;

(2) Disputes over payment arrears arising from the withholding of payments for agricultural and sideline products owed to farmer parties;

(3) Disputes over arrears of wages or labor remuneration for migrant workers, as well as labor dispute cases involving migrant workers with content of property delivery;

(4) Disputes over compensation for personal injury in agriculture-related cases;

(5) Other circumstances meeting the statutory conditions for advance enforcement.

Where there is a settlement dispute between the contractor and the project owner, but the fact of arrears of migrant workers' wages or labor remuneration is clear, and upon the contractor's application and the provision of guarantee according to law, the people's court may rule on advance enforcement for the part of the project payment involving migrant workers' wages or labor remuneration. However, certain measures shall be taken to ensure that wages and remuneration are paid in place.

9. For cases that require speedy trial and swift conclusion due to special circumstances such as strong seasonality in agricultural production, the people's court shall hear the case as soon as possible and render judgment promptly. Where necessary, it may rule on advance enforcement.

10. Civil disputes involving expropriation of rural collective land shall be handled according to law with caution and fairness, and the legitimate rights and interests of farmers whose land has been expropriated shall be effectively protected. For group disputes and other cases with wide scope and significant impact, meticulous and patient ideological work shall be done to prevent intensification of conflicts. Under the leadership of the local Party committee, supervision of the People's Congress, and support of the government, efforts shall be made to resolve conflicts locally and at the grassroots level.

11. In the trial of ordinary agriculture-related civil disputes such as marriage and family, inheritance, support, maintenance, and neighbor relations, the legitimate rights and interests of women, the elderly, and minors shall be effectively protected, various interest relationships and social relations shall be harmonized, family harmony, neighborly harmony, and rural civility shall be promoted, and the socialist moral code shall be carried forward.

12. In the trial of various types of agriculture-related civil dispute cases, the role of litigation mediation shall be fully utilized, and litigation mediation shall be carried through the entire process of case trial. Mediation efforts shall be intensified. Following the principle of "mediate where possible, adjudicate where necessary, combine mediation with adjudication, case closed and matter resolved," efforts shall be made to enhance the efficiency and quality of mediation work, and parties shall be facilitated as much as possible to reach mediation, achieving the elimination of conflicts, reduction of confrontation, and settlement of disputes, realizing the organic unity of legal and social effects, and avoiding mechanical handling of cases.

13. The function of administrative adjudication shall be fully utilized, and agriculture-related administrative cases such as illegal levying of fees and apportionment, land rights confirmation, collective land expropriation, housing demolition and resettlement compensation during land expropriation, and administrative compensation shall be correctly and promptly tried to protect the legitimate rights and interests of administrative counterparts according to law, and to safeguard and supervise administrative organs in exercising administrative functions according to law.

14. The enforcement work of agriculture-related cases shall be done well to ensure the timely realization of the legitimate rights and interests of farmers who have won their cases. Where a farmer party applies for enforcement, no advance enforcement fee shall be collected; such fee shall be deducted from the property after it is used to pay off debts. If the party subject to enforcement is also a farmer party and is in financial difficulty, the people's court may, upon its application, appropriately reduce or exempt the fee.

15. The adjudication force for agriculture-related cases shall be strengthened and augmented. Adjudicators with high professional standards, rich experience, and strong sense of responsibility shall be designated to handle agriculture-related cases. Where necessary, special collegial panels or dedicated personnel may be established to hear such cases.

III. Strengthen Trial Supervision and Petition Work for Agriculture-Related Cases

16. For petitioners whose cases are still under trial, they shall be informed to continue participating in the proceedings, and the relevant people's court shall be urged to render a timely trial according to law.

17. For petitions that meet the statutory conditions for retrial, or cases where a party applies for retrial, the retrial procedure shall be initiated according to law and in a timely manner. Once the retrial procedure has been entered, the case shall be concluded promptly according to law.

18. For habitual petitioners who unreasonably persist in petitioning, under the leadership of the local Party committee, the supervision of the People's Congress, and with the support and cooperation of the government and villagers' self-governing organizations, efforts shall be made to persuade them to accept the judgment and cease petitioning.

IV. Continue to Give Play to the Important Role of Basic People's Courts and Their Sent-Down People's Tribunals

19. The timely, simple, and swift institutional functions of the summary procedure in civil cases shall be fully utilized to improve trial efficiency, reduce the litigation costs of parties, and maximize the protection of the legitimate rights and interests of parties.

20. In accordance with the requirements of the Supreme People's Court's "Decision on Comprehensively Strengthening the Work of People's Tribunals," all construction tasks of people's tribunals shall be completed as soon as possible, laying a solid foundation for the work of people's tribunals to face the countryside, the grassroots, and the masses.

21. The practical significance of going deep into reality, into the grassroots, and among the masses shall be highly valued. The convenience spirit of the "Ma Xiwu trial method" shall be carried forward and enriched in keeping with the times. Circuit trial work shall be vigorously strengthened, especially in areas with inconvenient transportation and during the busy farming season. Where possible, the court shall go to the locality to hear cases on the spot, striving to achieve the effect of trying one case and educating a wide area.

V. Strengthen Guidance and Support for People's Mediation Organizations

22. People's mediation work shall be vigorously supported. The work guidance for rural grassroots people's mediation organizations shall be effectively strengthened and improved, and the level of guidance shall be enhanced. Effective ways of entrusting mediation to people's mediation organizations shall be actively explored. Judicial administrative organs shall be closely assisted and coordinated with, and various forms shall be adopted according to local conditions to strengthen the professional training of people's mediators and legal education work such as sending legal knowledge to the countryside.

23. Depending on the specific local circumstances, people's mediators may be arranged to participate in auxiliary work before trial, or experienced people's mediators may be appointed as people's assessors through prescribed procedures.

24. For agriculture-related civil cases involving people's mediation agreements, the validity of the mediation agreement shall be strictly confirmed in accordance with the Supreme People's Court's "Several Provisions on the Trial of Civil Cases Involving People's Mediation Agreements."

25. Close cooperation with relevant departments shall be maintained to broaden the channels for resolving agriculture-related civil disputes, and to explore and establish diversified, civilized, and harmonious alternative dispute resolution mechanisms.

August 21, 2006
